title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a base ring with a PD ideal S^+. A_S is a simplicial (bar-construction-like) object whose n-th term is a PD polynomial de Rham complex S{X_0,...,X_{n-1}}[dX_0,...,dX_{n-1}]. It is rewritten in the partial-sum coordinates U_r = X_0+...+X_r. These are the coordinates in which the faces and degeneracies of a nerve of the additive PD group G_a^# are simplest.

What is being classified. The previous pages classify maps phi_* : A_S -> A_{S'} that are morphisms of simplicial, graded-commutative algebras. They are not assumed a priori to respect either the cohomological grading or the divided powers. Such a map is encoded by three pieces of data:
- phi_0 : S -> S';
- a PD power series A'_1 = sum_{j>=1} a'_j X_0^{(j)}, the degree-0 part of phi(X_0);
- coefficients B'_i (i>=1), measuring the odd (degree-1) part of phi(X_0^{(i)}).

This page: reconstruction of phi_* from the data.
- phi_1 is given by phi_1(X_0^{(i)}) = A'_1^{(i)} + B'_i dX_0 and phi_1(dX_0) = dA'_1 = A'_1^{der} dX_0, where A'_1^{der} = sum a'_j X_0^{(j-1)}.
- phi_n is defined by the same formulas applied to each U_r separately.

NB on the condition 2B'_i = 0. Reading the image, it is not needed for phi_1 (only one odd generator, and dX_0^2 = 0). It is needed for n >= 2, so that images of commuting elements still commute. The source is commutative and the target graded-commutative. For a = a_0 + a_1 and b = b_0 + b_1 (even + odd parts), one has ab - ba = 2 a_1 b_1. So commutativity of phi(U_r^{(i)}) with phi(U_s^{(j)}) and with phi(dU_s), for r != s, requires 2 B'_i (...) dU_r dU_s = 0. The condition 2B'_i = 0 guarantees this.

Corollary 1. If 2 is invertible in S' (under one of three conditions from a remark after the theorem), then B'_i = 0, so phi_* respects the grading. If moreover S^+ = (t)_pd, phi_* also respects the divided powers.

Corollary 2.
- phi commutes with divided powers iff B'_i = A'_1^{(i-1)} B'_1 for all i. This is just gamma_i(A + B dX) = A^{(i)} + A^{(i-1)} B dX, using that dX is odd so its higher divided powers vanish.
- phi respects the gradings iff all B'_i = 0.

Purpose. This is a rigidity result: ring-theoretic endomorphisms of the PD de Rham complex (or of its simplicial bar version), viewed as plain algebras, are automatically compatible with grading and PD structure under mild hypotheses. It serves the 1976 IHES lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex and crystalline cohomology.
errors: The text writes (A_S)_n = S{U_0,...,U_n}[dU_0,...,dU_n], but only U_0,...,U_{n-1} were defined. This is an index slip: it should run to n-1 (or the indexing convention shifts).

Corollary 1 is conditional on unstated hypotheses ('one of the 3 conditions of the remark after the theorem'). From this page alone the deduction B'_i = 0 from 2 invertible needs 2B'_i = 0, which is only required when n >= 2. So the corollary relies on the simplicial levels n >= 2, not on phi_1.

ideas.what: Description of all dg-algebra (not necessarily PD or graded) morphisms between PD de Rham complexes of the PD affine line and its simplicial bar version, via data (phi_0, A'_1, B'_i)
ideas.modern_name: endomorphisms of the de Rham complex of G_a^#, or of functions on B G_a^#; rigidity of the PD de Rham complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: related themes in Drinfeld (prismatization, End(G_a^#)), Bhatt–Lurie, Moulinos–Robalo–Toën (filtered circle)

ideas.what: Criterion for PD compatibility: B'_i = A'^{(i-1)} B'_1
ideas.modern_name: divided powers of an even+odd sum (gamma_k(odd) = 0 for k >= 2)

ideas.what: Necessity of 2B'_i = 0 for commutativity in the graded-commutative target
ideas.modern_name: graded commutativity / sign issues in characteristic 2

missed.claim: The use of partial-sum coordinates U_r = X_0+...+X_r in a simplicial object of PD de Rham complexes suggests a cosimplicial/bar model of B G_a^# (or of a nerve of the PD additive group). This page studies its non-graded, non-PD automorphisms, i.e. how much structure is forced by the bare algebra structure. That anticipates modern questions on automorphisms of G_a^# and of the filtered circle / de Rham stack (Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie, Moulinos–Robalo–Toën), where the grading/filtration and PD structure are recovered from the ring object.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early instance of recovering grading and PD structure from a simplicial ring model of de Rham cohomology. A historian could link it to the prehistory of B G_a^# and HKR-filtered-circle approaches. The interpretation is tentative.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations on this page are routine. Their context, however, is interesting and unpublished: rigidity of the PD de Rham complex as a simplicial ring, including the 2-torsion subtlety. It loosely prefigures modern G_a^#/filtered-circle ideas, but the content itself is elementary.
transcription_corrections: NB line: the image reads roughly 'la condition 2B'_i=0 n'intervient pas pour la construction de phi_1, mais pour phi_n pour n>=2', not 'n'est nécessaire'.
Corollary 1: 'Si 2 est inversible dans S'' (primed S'), not S.
In the phi_n formulas, 'phi_n(U_+^{(i)})' should read 'phi_n(U_r^{(i)})'.
Corollary 1 continues: 'si de plus S^+=(t)_pd, phi_* respecte la structure de p.d.'; the underlined 'lorsque S^+=(t)_pd' is a marginal insertion.
Corollary 2 begins '(Pour que phi commute aux p.d.' (the parenthesis covers 'Pour'), consistent with the transcription.
